title: GitHub (2008) and the Pull Request as a Social Workflow
explainer: GitHub launched in 2008 and took the long-standing open-source habit of forking a project and sending back changes, then turned it into a structured, reviewable workflow built on top of Git's existing branching model: the pull request. GitHub's real contribution was not a change to how Git stores data, but a social and procedural layer for reviewing and merging other people's work, which is why 'a GitHub workflow' and 'Git itself' are often confused but are not the same thing.
